newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Small NZ debt mkt rally runs out of puff by close.
newsitem.headline: Small NZ debt mkt rally runs out of puff by close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* Morning rally runs out of steam by close
* Market starts pricing in bullish March qtr CPI number
New Zealand bond yields closed a couple of points lower on Tuesday but had given up ground gained in the morning as the market ran out of puff.
Dealers said the market had a tentative bid tone at the close with nervousness lingering about the currency.
Countering that is widespread bullishness in the short end that March quarter's CPI data due on April 15 will be below the Reserve Bank's forecast of 0.5 percent.
The tone in the bond market is neutral with direction still being set by global markets, dealers said.
Foreigner investors were selling the bank bill futures on the view that U.S. yields would continue to rise, they added.
"The (bill) market looks quite good technically from here. I think if the currency stays up at these levels it (futures) could break through resistance at 92.09," a bill dealer said.
The further rise of the U.S. dollar against the yen would support the Trade-Weighted Index even if the kiwi weakened, dealers said.
The bond market also came off as the Australian market started to soften, and traders saw yields staying rangebound until international markets give fresh impulse.

"I think the market is pretty neutral around here," said a Wellington bank chief dealer. "The market has defined a range of 25-30 (basis points over 8.00) on the topside in the long end (10-year bonds) and down towards the figure (8.00 percent) at the bottom end."
